question: Which family do GPT-style chat models belong to?
options: Encoder-only
Encoder-decoder
Decoder-only
Convolutional
explanation: GPT models are stacks of causally masked transformer blocks trained to predict the next token.

question: In cross-attention, where do the queries and the keys/values come from?
options: Queries from the decoder, keys and values from the encoder output
All three from the decoder
All three from the encoder
Queries from the encoder, keys and values from the decoder
explanation: The decoder asks the questions; the encoder output (memory) is scored and averaged.

question: In the lesson, changing the last two tokens left the first seven decoder outputs exactly unchanged. Why does that matter?
options: It shows the decoder is not trained
It proves the causal mask works, so all positions can be trained in parallel without seeing the token they must predict
It means the decoder ignores its input
It shows the encoder is broken
explanation: Because no information flows from later to earlier positions, next-token training on every position at once is honest, and step-by-step generation behaves identically.

question: The decoder-only and encoder-only addition models had exactly the same number of parameters. What differs between them?
options: Only the attention mask and how the answer positions are arranged and filled
The encoder has no feed-forward layers
The decoder has cross-attention
The encoder uses RNNs
explanation: Both are the same Stack plus a linear head. One uses a causal mask and generates; the other attends both ways and fills blanks in one pass.

question: Why are open-ended text generators decoders rather than encoders that fill all positions at once?
options: Encoders cannot be trained with cross-entropy
Decoders have more parameters
Encoders are slower
Each generated token depends on the previous choices; predicting all positions independently cannot coordinate them when many outputs are valid
explanation: For addition each digit is determined by the input, so parallel prediction works. For text, autoregressive generation conditions each token on the ones already chosen.

question: Why were 2,000 addition problems held out from training?
options: To make training faster
Because the vocabulary cannot represent them
To test whether the model learned addition rather than memorizing the training table
Because nn.Transformer requires a validation set
explanation: Near-perfect accuracy on problems never seen in training shows the models generalize.
